scope: Close the workflows already exposed by Product Atelier without adding new product capabilities.

state_policy.pwc2_entry_requirement: Before PWC-2 implementation, classify every state used by the two P0 production workflows as durable or ephemeral and approve its recovery owner.
durable_when_any: Loss changes a user-visible business result or its provenance.
Loss discards committed user-authored work, an explicit decision, or a reusable business artifact.
Loss breaks task, result, canvas, local-edit, export, or paid-call accountability.
Loss prevents safe recovery from the last committed checkpoint without repeating paid work.
mandatory_durable_families: accepted task input, brief, parameters, and result lineage
task attempts, terminal state, and recoverable paid-work checkpoints
committed canvas content and document versions
committed ROI, mask, local-edit specification, and composition receipt
review decisions, governed knowledge decisions, and applied-rule trace
export identity needed to reproduce or audit a delivery
ephemeral_when_all: It can be reconstructed from durable state without a provider call.
Its loss does not discard user-authored business work or a user decision.
Its loss does not change lineage, billing accountability, delivery, or recovery safety.
rules: Do not persist UI state merely because it exists.
Assess user-authored drafts and canvas viewport context explicitly before classifying them.
Unclassified state must not be promised as restart-safe.

requirements: Before authorization, the UI states the paid operation and its maximum bounded call scope.
The authorization receipt records authorization id, user action, scope, maximum calls, workflow or job id, operation family, timestamp, and consumption.
Every provider attempt references the authorization receipt that permits it.
A failed or billing-unknown attempt cannot trigger another paid attempt automatically.
A user-initiated retry requires a still-valid remaining authorization or a new explicit authorization.

evidence_classes.automated: Contract, state transition, idempotency, failure injection, ledger invariant, and artifact identity checks.
evidence_classes.packaged_manual: A human completes the specified interaction in the exact packaged candidate and verifies visible identity and result continuity.
evidence_classes.live_provider: A bounded real-provider canary whose attempt count and authorization receipts are reconciled before validation.

workflows.entry: A durable imported product asset is selected in the single-product workflow.
workflows.exit: The original result and its reviewed adjustment are traceable, exportable, and recoverable after restart.
steps: create an immediate adjustment as a child version
restart and reopen the same result lineage
acceptance: Original results are never overwritten by an adjustment.
Review, adjustment, provider attempt, and export reference the same lineage.
Only durable state is required to survive restart.
A failed paid attempt does not retry automatically.

workflows.entry: A durable image or result node with a valid asset reference is selected in the spatial canvas.
workflows.exit: A fine-edit child result is committed, returned to the originating spatial canvas, exported, and recoverable after restart.
steps: commit ROI, mask, and local-edit specification
compose the candidate into a child canvas version
return the child result to the originating spatial canvas
acceptance: Excalidraw owns spatial composition and Fabric owns pixel editing.
Every handoff preserves asset, task, result, canvas, and local-edit references.
A handoff failure preserves the committed child result and offers a working recovery action.
Only the explicitly classified durable state survives restart.

workflows.entry: A workspace, canvas, task, asset, or provider dependency fails or becomes stale.
workflows.exit: The user can understand the failure, choose a valid next action, and recover or stop without data loss or hidden paid work.
steps: show cause, impact, paid-call status, and next action
retry read, retry save, reload conflict, resume task, or stop as appropriate
reconcile durable state and provider attempts
acceptance: No error action is a no-op for the state that displayed it.
An empty view cannot silently represent a failed read.
Blocked state is scoped to the failed capability and is recoverable.
Billing-unknown and failed provider attempts never trigger automatic paid retry.

workflows.entry: The user starts an already-exposed multi-file, group-split, batch-cutout, semantic-selection, or outpaint workflow.
workflows.exit: The batch or derived results are individually traceable, partially recoverable, and delivered to the declared output location.
acceptance: A multi-file run proves more than one independent item.
Partial failure, cancel, resume, and item-level retry preserve completed outputs.
Semantic grounding failure offers manual selection without a hidden provider call.
Outpaint writes only its authorized output region and transition band.

workflows.entry: A product profile or result review is committed.
workflows.exit: Version binding and governed knowledge application are visible in the next task trace without rewriting history.
acceptance: Profile version updates never rebind historical tasks silently.
Pending suggestions do not affect task compilation.
Approved suggestions appear in applied-rule trace and disabled suggestions do not.
Historical review and knowledge evidence remains immutable.

tasks.title: Failure taxonomy and recovery action map
tasks.deliverable: One shared mapping for read, save, conflict, reference, contract, runtime, task, and provider failures, including preservation and paid-call status.

tasks.title: Fabric workspace recovery semantics
tasks.deliverable: Separate working actions for initial read failure, save retry, conflict reload, and fine-edit prerequisite failure.

tasks.title: Spatial canvas recovery semantics
tasks.deliverable: Explicit list, open, save, conflict-copy, and retry states; a failed list cannot render as an empty library.

tasks.title: Cross-canvas handoff safety
tasks.deliverable: Recoverable spatial-to-Fabric entry and Fabric-to-spatial return without losing committed child results or blocking unrelated workspaces.

tasks.title: Recovery acceptance and packaged evidence
tasks.deliverable: Automated fault-injection coverage plus packaged human verification of every visible recovery action.
